tone_markers: First-person experiments with Elsa when testing food or treats
Plain questions that invite owners to answer with their own routines
Warm, lightly funny understatement instead of hard sell
Trust comes from showing the real dog behavior, including rejection or messiness

deck_guardrails.text: Beautiful design that people love having on the countertop

do_rules: Start from a real dog, routine, or owner question.
Use product language only after the care moment is clear.
Make uncertainty and validation feel honest.
Borrow audience words only when the evidence source is attached.
avoid_rules: Do not write generic superfood language.
Do not turn grief or senior care into a sales hook.
Do not imply medical outcomes beyond the brief's allowed claims.
Do not flatten The Dogist voice into polished wellness-brand copy.
